newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC shares drop on downgrading.
newsitem.headline: NEC shares drop on downgrading.

text.p: Shares of NEC Corp dropped in active trade on Tuesday morning after being downgraded by Nomura Securities Co Ltd, traders said.
At 0044 GMT, the price of the leading high-tech enterprise was down 40 yen at 1,560. Volume was 3.369 million shares, making the firm the heaviest traded issue on the Tokyo bourse.
On Monday, Nomura Securities downgraded NEC to a "2" rating from its previous "1".

In its three-grade rating system, Nomura assigns a 2 rating to issues whose values it sees moving within 10 percentage points in either direction of the key 225-share Nikkei average over the next six months.
According to Nomura, NEC's investment in Packard Bell NEC (PB-NEC) was accumulating and there was a risk that the firm might not be able to recover its investment.
Nomura also said the effect of a fall in DRAM prices on NEC's earnings could not be ignored.
